summary: Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Ngawang Nyima studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Ngawang Sherpa earned a PhD in Buddhist studies at Florida State University in 2022. That same year, he held a post in religion at Florida State University, working in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology.

Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen. He taught numerous students, including Ngulchu Yangchen Drubpai Dorje.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Nguyen Thi Tuyet completed a PhD at Punjabi University, where she was supervised by Inder Mohan Singh, and studied under the traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet (attested 2012).
Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned a PhD at Punjabi University under the doctoral supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he was supervised by Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor Karam Tej Singh Sarao.

Nguyễn Ngọc Ánh studied at VNU-HCM (BA 2011–2015), the University of Delhi (MA 2016–2018), and the University of Economics and Law (LLB 2021–2023). In 2020, he held a PhD scholar post at the University of Colombo.
Nhu Lien specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under Ādiccavaṃsa.
Working in religious studies and Buddhist studies, Nhung Lu Rots studied at the University of Oslo (attested 2026) and served there as a postdoctoral researcher in 2026.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia (~1946–1965), Gongga Rinpoche, and Hsu Yun. He served as head at Central People's Broadcasting Station and professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) studied at Rissho University (1912), Taisho University, Koyasan University, Horyuji Kangakuin, and Kennin-ji. He founded Nipponzan-Myohoji, taught Gyoryo Maruyama, and worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies.

Nicholas Dirks studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981). Working in indology and history/archaeology, he held posts at Caltech (~1982–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2012).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) studied at the University of Oxford under Rodney Needham. Working in indology and religious studies, he held posts at Durham University (1972–1976), SOAS (1969–1971), and Oxford, including as Reader (1976, 1997).

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1916–1921). A specialist in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, he held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1923–1941) and as Professor of Mongolian at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts (1893–1897). He directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts (~1906–1917) and founded the Master Institute of United Arts (1921).

Nicholas Thanissaro studied at the University of Manchester (BSc 1982–1985), Manchester Metropolitan University (1985–1986), the University of Warwick (PhD 2010–2016), and the University of South Wales (MA 2017), working in Buddhist studies and religious studies.

Nicholas Witkowski earned his PhD at Stanford University (-2015). A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at the University of Tokyo (2015–2017), Nanyang Technological University (2018), and the University of San Diego (2022).
Nicholson T. Collier works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.
